subject.title: All LLM API calls time out simultaneously despite APIs being reachable (multi-agent concurrency issue)

question: Is current source and related PR evidence enough to treat the simultaneous Telegram-provider timeout report as mitigated, or should maintainers require a fresh current-main four-agent Telegram reproduction before choosing a code change?
rationale: The evidence spans Telegram runner concurrency, provider transport, model fallback, runtime timeout policy, and launch/runtime defaults; automation should not choose the owner boundary or declare the issue fixed without maintainer proof expectations.

options.title: Require current-main live repro
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a current-main four-agent Telegram trace before promoting a fix or close decision.

options.title: Promote a narrower owner issue
options.body: Move the remaining work to a maintainer-authored Telegram/runtime/provider bottleneck issue if maintainers want a more specific canonical tracker.

options.title: Accept mitigation as enough after proof
options.body: Close only if a current-main run shows the original simultaneous timeout pattern no longer occurs under comparable load.

recommendation.title: Require current-main live repro
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a current-main four-agent Telegram trace before promoting a fix or close decision.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has repeated history on the model fallback surface and is the best available routing owner for a cross-agent/runtime proof decision.
